sentences.text: 2  JUDGMENT Dated this the 10th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.250 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kottayam is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.09.2007.

According to the petitioner, on 19.09.2007 at about 9.15 a.m, he was riding pillion on a motorcycle,
bearing Registration No.KL 5U/4323, ridden by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which, he lost control over the motorcycle and thereby the motorcycle capsized and he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the registered owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the age, occupation, monthly income of the petitioner and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,01,340/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.
8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
9. Heard Sri.Philip T. Varghese the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, and Sri.P.G Ganappan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

Shan vs Renjith.P.R on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155341070/
2 M.A.C.A No.2757of 2014 11.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"(1) Comminuted fracture lower end of radius, (2) fracture ulnar styloid with dislocation of left inferior radio- ulnar joint, (3) fracture scaphoid left wrist, (4) abrasion forehead to (Rt) eye (3x2 cm), (5) swelling and deformity (Rt) wrist, (6) abrasion over (Rt) eye-brow (2x1 cm), (7) contusion chest, (8) abrasion (Rt) forehead, (9) swelling on the forehead (right), (10) mobility of two teeth and (11) bleeding from mouth and nose."
12.
The disability Certificate issued by PW1 assessed the permanent physical disability of the petitioner at 12%.

However, the Tribunal has scaled down the disability of the petitioner to 5%,
without assigning valid and cogent reasons.
The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.
(Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability certificate.
In the above circumstances, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as fixed by PW1 at 12% is liable to be accepted.

13. As per the dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during M.A.C.A No.2757of 2014 the year 2007 will come to Rs.6000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, for the purpose of assessing the compensation under section 163A of the M.V.Act, the annual income of the petitioner is fixed as Rs.40,000/-.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 23 years.
Therefore, the multiplier to be applied is18, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.86,400/- (40,000/- x 18 x 12/100).
15. Towards loss of earning, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.13,200/-, being the notional income of the petitioner for a period of four months.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by him, I hold that the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of six months.
Therefore, towards loss of earning, the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
16. Though the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings', the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.5,000/- only on that head.
Since no medical bills were produced, he is not entitled get the compensation towards medical expenses.
17. Towards loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/- was awarded.

As argued by the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent, the claim petition under Section M.A.C.A No.2757of 2014 163A, the victim is not Shan vs Renjith.P.R on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155341070/
3 entitled to get any compensation under the head loss of amenities and as such Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head loss of amenities will be deducted.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.1,13,900/- as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal  (in Rs.)

1 Loss of earnings 13200 20,000  2 Transport to hospital 1000 1000  3 Extra nourishment 1000 1000  5 Pain and sufferings 25,000 5,000  6 Compensation for 35,640 86,400  permanent disability  7 Compensation for loss of 25,000 Nil  amenities  Total 1,01,340/- 1,13,900/-
 Enhanced Amount = 12,560/-
 M.A.C.A No.2757of 2014 20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.1,13,900/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirteen Thousand Nine Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 577 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
